headline: All-remote DevSecOps platform builder emphasizing contribution, inclusion, and distributed work—now adding AI to its mission.
identity: GitLab has consistently valued remote work, inclusive contribution, and transparency across its careers messaging from 2015 onward. The company's language around "everyone can contribute" and all-remote operations has remained steady and even strengthened through 2022, with altruism and inclusion language rising sharply from 2018–2022 (zscore +1.23 and +0.33 respectively). However, craft language—how the company describes the quality and rigor of work itself—dipped notably in 2023 (zscore -2.61), suggesting a shift away from emphasizing craftsmanship. AI language emerged only in 2025–2026, with the platform now framed as "AI-powered" and the mission updated to address "the agentic era," marking a significant pivot in how GitLab positions its product and culture.
fit: You might be a good fit if you are someone who values autonomy, asynchronous work, and the ability to contribute meaningfully across roles and geographies. GitLab's language consistently reaches for people comfortable with remote-first operations, transparency, and a mission-driven sense of impact—though recent messaging suggests they're also seeking people ready to work in an AI-augmented environment.

sections.heading: Remote work and contribution as core identity (2015–2022)
sections.body:
From its earliest careers pages, GitLab has anchored itself in all-remote operations and a philosophy that "everyone can contribute." This language appeared in 2015 and persisted through 2022 with increasing emphasis. Altruism scores rose from -1.44 (2015) to +1.23 (2022), driven by repeated framing of the mission: "Our mission makes it clear that we believe in a world where everyone can contribute" (2022). Inclusion language similarly climbed from near-absent in 2015–2017 to explicit and structural by 2018, with dedicated mentions of LGBTQ+ channels, women in tech sponsorships, and team member resource groups. By 2021, the careers copy added "belonging" language alongside diversity and inclusion, signaling a shift from demographic representation to cultural integration.

Wellbeing messaging also strengthened during this period, peaking in 2022 (zscore +1.31) with employee stories emphasizing flexibility for caregiving, travel, and personal autonomy. The company's handbook—described as "over 3000 pages" by 2021—became a recurring symbol of transparency and accessibility.

sections.heading: A dip in craft language and the 2023 inflection (2023)
sections.body: In 2023, GitLab's careers copy underwent a notable contraction and tonal shift. Craft language (how the company describes the quality and rigor of work) fell to zscore -2.61, the lowest in the dataset. Inclusion language also dropped sharply (zscore -1.97). The copy became more product-focused and less people-focused: instead of stories about culture and contribution, the 2023 pages emphasized "GitLab by the numbers" and the DevSecOps platform itself. This may reflect a transition period—the company was preparing for a new narrative frame—but it represents a clear departure from the 2018–2022 emphasis on belonging and craft.

sections.heading: AI and the agentic era (2025–2026)
sections.body: AI language entered GitLab's careers messaging in 2025 at 12.5% prevalence and jumped to 25% by 2026. The platform is now described as "the most comprehensive AI-powered DevSecOps platform" and "the trusted enterprise platform for software creation in the AI era." The mission statement evolved: by 2026, it reads "unlock every team to ship software at the speed of imagination" and explicitly references "the pace the agentic era demands." A new operating principle—"Culture of Excellence"—was introduced alongside the existing CREDIT values. Inclusion language rebounded in 2025–2026 (zscore +1.03), with emphasis on "creating inclusive environments" and "spaces where everyone belongs." Notably, the company added a line about using AI in the interview process "while keeping people at the centre of hiring decisions," signaling an attempt to balance automation with human judgment. Techno-optimism language, which had been muted in 2023–2025, also recovered in 2026 (zscore +0.83).
